correctness.summary: For three colours on a path or cycle, a forceable omitted set is exactly an independent set of degree-2 vertices whose two neighbours have distinct colours in the final colouring. Encoding proper 3-colourings by plus/minus-one edge increments over Z_3 gives the path count directly and reduces the cycle count to a roots-of-unity filter. Boundary cases and exhaustive coefficient checks through order 8 agree with the formulas.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2026 source establishes basic forced-colouring theory, a two-colour connected-bipartite formula, and small examples, but no general three-colour path/cycle formulas were found. The inspected 2024 arXiv version of the 2025 Farr--Morgan chapter also contains no such family formula. Exact and synonymous searches found no equivalent or stronger coverage. The final typeset 2025 chapter was not checked page-by-page and remains the closest residual risk.

value.summary: The result determines the first nontrivial forced-colouring regime for two canonical infinite graph families, explains it through tight independent sets, gives a path recurrence and a cycle closure correction, and combines with known or elementary regimes to determine the forced-colouring function of every path and cycle for every positive integer number of colours.

limitations: The structural characterization uses maximum degree 2 and is not claimed for general graphs.
The final typeset 2025 Farr--Morgan chapter was not inspected page-by-page; an addition absent from its arXiv version remains a residual originality risk.
Very recent or unindexed parallel work may exist.
The exhaustive computation is supporting evidence and does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
